source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions: this is collective-initialization scenario variant 79. Backend, launcher and versions, expected world size, host placement, scheduler, container permissions, fabric, selected interfaces, topology, and the exact blocked stage are unknown; measure them rather than infer them. Use an isolated authorized allocation, redact endpoints and credentials, set a bounded watchdog, and guarantee process cleanup. Capture a run ID, host/rank/local-rank/world size, PID, configuration and software hashes, rendezvous/store endpoints and membership, per-rank collective entry/exit and last-progress timestamps, stderr, transport diagnostics, and GPU/NIC identifiers. Verify that every expected rank starts exactly once, membership and endpoint agree, all ranks enter collectives in identical order, GPU visibility and rank-to-device mapping are unique, driver/runtime/backend compatibility holds, peer access and PCIe/NVLink topology are healthy, and container device access, shared memory, ulimits, NIC/address/route/DNS/MTU/firewall settings are usable.

Falsifiable hypothesis: a rank-specific rendezvous membership or selected transport path defect prevents all participants from entering the same collective. Support it only if repeated matched trials show the same rank/path-specific missing or late membership, failed connectivity, or transport error and the symptom improves after one authorized membership or interface correction; reject it if failures move across ranks or persist with verified membership and an alternate path. Do not infer causality from one run.

Controlled experiment: first run a minimal checksum-validated all-reduce with the same launcher, world size, rank mapping, environment, and bounded timeout. Randomize repeated trials across single-node, reduced-world, and full-world placements while blocking unrelated configuration changes. Record success, timeout, rank failure, checksum/correctness, latency, and cleanup separately. Compare default versus explicitly selected interfaces only in an isolated allocation; keep backend, message size, software, topology, and process limits fixed. A single-node pass localizes suspicion toward cross-host rendezvous or transport but does not prove it; a reduced-world pass does not establish full-world correctness. Also test competing explanations: collective-order divergence, duplicate/missing ranks, wrong GPU visibility, topology/peer-access faults, driver/runtime/backend mismatch, NIC routes/MTU/firewall/DNS, shared-memory or ulimit exhaustion, and resource or scheduler failures.

Mitigation and rollback: fail fast on incomplete membership, duplicate ranks, invalid device mapping, or missing endpoint reachability; use documented interface/address selection and a finite timeout, not indefinite retries. Preserve redacted logs, terminate only the owned process group after timeout, clean rendezvous state, and restore the previous configuration immediately if correctness, timeout rate, latency, or cleanup regresses. Promote a fix only after repeated matched trials meet predeclared correctness and timeout/latency gates; otherwise keep the diagnosis provisional and require domain-expert review.
